questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere that was very gothic and that gave Hogwarts vibe with interesting subjects, and I got that from university of Glasgow

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there were some administrative issues

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. The univerisity of Glasgow was good at helping and they gave very useful information. there was also a welcoming team (online) and if one wanted to then you could book an introduction or something like that (I didn't do that)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had to watch some videos about how it would be to study there and just an introduction in general to choosing courses etc. Really helped with any confusion

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
There were however some issues with the administration. They took in 2000 people too many, and they mixed up my classes so I got 2 almost identical ones. it was hard getting in contact with them because there were so many people experiencing issues and the wait was up to 7 days. When I finally got in contact witht hem then i was given a choice of 3  subjects (all law) (none of which I wanted) and i had to pick one because I needed the ECTS points. I then had to write home to my home univerisyt to check if they could tranfers my points for the new classes because I had not gotten the other one pre approved. They said that it would probraly not be a problem, but I had to just take the class and hope that it got approved. luckely it got approved, but it was very stressfull. therefore I did not have all of my classes until it was the end of week 2/ start of week 3. I know many other exchange students also didn't get enrolled in the right courses (like me) and some couldn't see their schedule. There were therefore many issues with the administration, but once it got settled then it was fine. it was just a bit stressful and uncomfortable for 2 weeks, and honestly, I was never supposed to have had 2 identical classes (I was told it shouldn't even be an option), and since it took them so long then I couldn't get the ones I wanted because by then they were already booked up, so I kind of ended up having the classes that no one wanted

All in all then everything else was fine, but there was a huge mess with the classes and schedules for the exchange students (most likely because of covid).

When I finally got in contact with someone, then they were very kind and helpfull

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
This was a bit hard. I had to get an air BnB because I couldn't find any housing at all. I would recommend that you book housing right away (when you know you've gotten accepted) because it gets booked super quickly. there was also a need for housing in the city because they took in 2000 too many, so this was really a bit of a problem. I was also told that the uni wouldn't give accommodation to the one-semester students from Denmark so I had to go around them. 

the student housing is in general fine, but it could be better. I would recommend unite students etc 

I was so lucky and lived with a man called paul up in Maryhill and had a great time! But I know others who could find no housing and be living in hostels trying to find stuff and others who had horrible experiences with Airbnb. there were also a lot of scams going on, people faking that they needed a roommate or fake Airbnb so the people who fell for it (almost me) lost money on it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can give you a different experience because you aren't necessarily living with other people, and it can be really expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to book a visa check (but since I'm from Denmark then i didn't need one) and then just meet up at the slot I booked. very easy. also got my student ID here, and they could take my photo

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to book a slot so they could check your visa, you meet up at the time and place, they check it and you are good to go.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always ask people who where there to help or you could email the visiting students team

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got 2 out of 3 classes that I wanted... i got to almost identical ones (one was scots law and the other were common law but in the same subject(criminal law)) and because of this mistake then when they had to move me then the other 4 classes that I had requested as backup (in case I didn't get the ones I really wanted) were already filled up, so I had to choose from the ones that were left... this really sucked because I couldn't do anything different, it was the University who had made a mistake...
I know this happened to multiple people or other issues in the same genre, such as not being able to see your schedule, not being on the moodle page etc etc...

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice that you apply for 5-6 courses even though you might need less (I needed 3), just in case your class gets booked! I did this myself but because of the administrative mistake then I didn't matter in the end, but it is still a good idea, because if everything had worked as it should, then I would most likely get all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got healthcare law, introduction to roman law and criminal law of England and wales. i liked them all, but some of them were easier than others since some were for first years. In general, I learned stuff but I was also doing a lot of other stuff (experiencing the country etc.)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was somewhat the same if not easier. I would not pick classes where you are supposed to know something about the English constitution etc, since we don't know about that in Denmark (not a part of our legal education), but if it is learning something completely new (like healthcare law or criminal law or roman law), then the level seemed the same or easier in spite of it being in English/Scottish

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
We had lectures and tutorials. lecture= forelæsning, tutorial= seminarundervisning. 
healthcare; had only lectures where we were about 50 people ca. 
criminal law; had lectures where we where the entire year and tutorials where we were about 10-15 people on each team
roman law; this was a year 4 class, so we were about 20 people ( reminds me very much of "seminar" as back home)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Principles of Healthcare Law
Criminal Law of England and Wales
introduction to Roman world

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend first year classes if you want to have time to experience other stuff, but I would recomend year.3 or 4 if you want to study-study

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used Uber a lot. I broke my foot so had to be transported around so that was a bit more expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinks are only 4-6 pounds but a bottle of gin is 18 pounds in a supermarket

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many clubs, it's crazy! So a great way to meet new people but also just doing the stuff you love

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there where book clubs, sports clubs, movie clubs, social clubs, fandom clubs, baking clubs etc etc! so many options

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining a club if you want to make friends easily! I met one of my closest friends at a mature student mixer and my other friend group I met at Taylor swift/ Shrek karaoke event that the 2 clubs held! if you are kind and open-minded then there are a lot of people who want to be friends! there are also many students in town; I met a girl at a coffee shop where we just chatted, so it is also possible to meet people off campus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
the highlands, Edinburgh is only a train ride away! I went on trips with international students ( I would not recommend viva tours) and it was so fun! I saw Scotland for a cheap price, and I made new friends! I went on maybe 6-7 tours like that and I always did it alone and at the end of the day, I always made at least one new friend!! it is possible to do it alone and still enjoy stuff, so I would say go for it!

would also recommend Luss, it's not that far away and the nature is pretty if you pick a good hiking route

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was super easy! there is not much of a change except that the cars are driving on the other side of the road

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be kind and open! Join clubs and not just the erasmus club!! and speak to your fellow students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none really, only the car thing (which is minor)! and the clubs close a bit early

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the kindness and it was fun hearing about the Scottish culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: found housing (early), be openminded and it can be a bit lonely at times (and that is okay)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: i really enjoyed naked soup, i went there every thursday with my friends for a cheap lunch and it is such a great vibe

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really pushed my boundaries and learned so much about myself. I feel more independent since I have lived in another country and studied in it!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the academics and the making of friends. You have to put yourself out there in a different way and you are on 24/7 but I think it is worth it

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy the time, it really flies!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
